cost_of_karts_on_the_server.scenario: red_engine2 perf, 8 players, 2 s windows, best of 3, same scene with and without the race block
cost_of_karts_on_the_server.reading: Kart driving, bumps and race tracking add about 1-2 us per tick for 8 karts (noise level). The network cost is exact: 87 bytes per snapshot (7 header + 8 x 10) at 30 snapshots per second = +2.6 KB/s per client.

prediction_over_loopback.scenario: tests/net_race.rs a_real_client_predicts_its_kart_and_the_server_agrees_with_it: real Server thread, real Bot (network client + predictor), 5 s, kart driving straight after a 1 s countdown
prediction_over_loopback.reading: The one correction is the light going green: the server releases the kart a moment before the client hears about it. A client that extrapolates the start from the server tick would remove it.
prediction_over_loopback.unit_level: net::predict tests: with 6 ticks of lag and reconciliation every 4 ticks, all eight drivers (steering, drifting, hopping, a wall) make ZERO corrections and end bit-identical to the server.

bot_balance_lap_times.scenario: tests/kart_bots.rs balance_lap_times_per_animal: one level-1.0 bot alone on the plain diamond (radius 40, four 90-degree corners, no walls, no items), three laps, dev-profile CLI
bot_balance_lap_times.spread: best 49.2 s, worst 59.2 s: the slowest is 20% behind the fastest
bot_balance_lap_times.reading: On this track top speed dominates. Bunny (best acceleration and handling, top speed 22) is 6% slower than the balanced Duck, and Beaver and Bear (top speed 21-22, slow steering) trail. Nothing here counts pickups, drifting payoffs on real corners, off-road, or the drivers' abilities, so this is a floor for tuning, not a verdict: a track with tight corners and dirt shortcuts should favour Bunny and Coyote.

bot_race_with_items.scenario: 8 bots at level 0.9, 3 laps, four item boxes on the gate points, 3 s respawn
bot_race_with_items.reading: Bots pick up items and use them, but hits are rare (2 in a full race). The Beaver bot laid no planks: it is the slowest kart, so nobody is behind it to punish, which is the correct behaviour of the trigger and a design finding (Build rewards a fast, leading Beaver). Acorn accuracy or a wider 'ahead' window would raise hit counts if the game wants more chaos.
